claims.content: First-principles studies of coherent two-phase composites are rare.
claims.evidence_span: Papers related to first-principles calculations of these two-phase coherent nanocomposites are rather rare as most of the previous studies focused on individual phases

claims.content: Fe-Al alloys lose ductility and high-temperature strength.
claims.evidence_span: their wider use is hindered by their low ductility at ambient temperatures and a drop of the strength at elevated temperatures

claims.content: The study addresses the gap by analyzing two-phase interfaces.
claims.evidence_span: In order to fill in this gap, we study in this work thermodynamic, structural and elastic properties of interfaces between these two phases

claims.content: Lateral stress linearly raises tensile strength.
claims.evidence_span: the tensile strength σ ts for all structures linearly increases with increasing of the lateral stress σ lt
the thermal vibrations significantly decrease the tensile strength

claims.content: Uniaxial deformation generates nearly hydrostatic loading.
claims.evidence_span: the uniaxial deformation (OUD) leads to nearly identical values of all three normal stresses, i.e., σ x = σ y = σ ax , means that the loading is almost hydrostatic

claims.content: Heating to 300 K cuts Fe3Al strength to about 12.5 GPa.
claims.evidence_span: the strength decreases from 16.7 GPa (obtained from the T = 1 K simulations) to values approx. 12.5 GPa for temperature 300 K, i.e., only 75 %

claims.content: Defect-free simulations may overestimate tensile strength.
claims.evidence_span: we have simulated behavior of defect-free systems while some crystal defects or instabilities might lower the tensile strength
